sections.overview: Phoebis philea is a large sulphur butterfly of the American tropics, ranging from Mexico to Argentina.
sections.identification: Males are yellow with a broad orange forewing band; females vary from whitish to yellow and also show orange markings.
sections.habitat: It uses open areas and forest edges; in Colombia it has been recorded from sea level to about 2000 m.
sections.diet: Caterpillars feed on legumes, especially Senna and other cassias. Adults take flower nectar.
sections.behavior: It is a strong, fast flyer and often visits flowers; in Florida it also frequents gardens and parks.
sections.reproduction: Females lay eggs singly on host plants, and the caterpillars feed on those plants.
sections.ecology: It resembles the Cloudless Sulphur (Phoebis sennae), but the latter lacks the orange markings above.
sections.conservation: The sources consulted describe a broad range but do not provide a current global conservation assessment.
